clue.text: English wearing sacks for clothes

indicators.note: the word for sacking has the English abbreviation on it, as a garment worn round it

parts.note: to sack a town is to rob it, so sacks means robs

explanation.surface: An English person dressed in old sacks for want of proper clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Robes are long loose garments, so they are a kind of clothing.

clue.text: Who's Tommy, having wobble over quiet period?

parts.note: to rock is to sway or wobble
O is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for an over
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about someone called Tommy wobbling after a quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The Who is a rock band, and Tommy is their 1969 album telling one story through songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy by the band The Who is the classic example of a sung stage-style album, a rock opera.

clue.text: Bung second-class cheese sandwiches?

indicators.note: the cheese holds the letter between its parts like a sandwich filling

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
B is the grade below A, so second-class

explanation.surface: A shopper suggests stuffing cheap cheese sandwiches into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Bung is British slang for a bribe, a payment made to win favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is informal British slang for an illicit payment made to secure favour.

clue.text: Boys without power or patron

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the boys go around the letter

parts.note: sons are boys
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between their boys, who have no clout, and a wealthy patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is a backer who supports a person or event financially, just as a patron does.

clue.text: See 17
Dodger Luke finally seen with Anakin?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Luke

parts.note: Anakin Skywalker becomes Darth Vader in Star Wars

explanation.surface: A Star Wars question: is Luke at last seen alongside his father Anakin?
explanation.walkthrough: In Star Wars, Anakin Skywalker, Luke's father, becomes Darth Vader.
explanation.definitionFit: An evader is someone who dodges something, such as tax or a question.

clue.text: Rooms that crossword solver may use?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the dictionary favoured by crossword solvers

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a British dictionary much used by crossword setters and solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are rooms, and Chambers is also the name of a reference dictionary popular with puzzlers.

clue.text: CD-i Lily redesigned is wonderful

indicators.note: something redesigned is put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises an old CD-i disc about someone called Lily after its makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: CD-i was an interactive compact disc format of the early 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllic describes something perfect and blissful, so it is close to wonderful.

clue.text: Cunning fellows housed in suitable accommodation

indicators.note: the cunning fellows are lodged inside the word for suitable

parts.note: apt means suitable
art can mean cunning or craftiness
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Crafty men living in fitting lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms used as a home, so it is a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Excited atmosphere around street

indicators.note: the word for atmosphere goes round the street abbreviation

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A buzzing mood hangs over a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means in a state of excited movement or bustle.

clue.text: Sausage with it dunked in drink? Thanks!

indicators.note: dunked in means plunged inside the drink

parts.note: cola is a fizzy drink
hip means fashionable, with it
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone thanked for a sausage that, oddly, has been dipped in a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: With it is a single unit meaning trendy, not two link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, common in Britain.

clue.text: Riser lively at last — whence comes the dawn?

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of lively

parts.note: the sun rises in the east

explanation.surface: An early riser finally lively, asking where the sunrise comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is a raising agent that makes dough rise, so it is a riser.

clue.text: Manage poetry in Old English

indicators.note: in places the poetry inside the abbreviation

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone who manages a body of Anglo-Saxon poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or run, which is to manage.

clue.text: Support from belts or elastic?

indicators.note: elastic things stretch and change shape, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A query about whether support comes from belts or from elastic.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, a synonym for support; a bolster is also a long pillow.

clue.text: Bear brings death to Yorkshire river

parts.note: end can mean death
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: A bear causes a death by a Yorkshire river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to bear or tolerate something unpleasant.

clue.text: Withdraw flawed design before time

indicators.note: a flawed thing is broken up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A faulty design is pulled before its deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is a common crossword signal for a short word for a long period; here it follows the rearranged design.
explanation.definitionFit: To disengage is to pull back or detach, which is to withdraw.

clue.text: Severe reprimand in court for 29 hero

indicators.note: in places the reprimand within the court abbreviation

parts.note: a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: A hero from clue 29 gets a dressing-down in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 29 is ALAMO; Davy Crockett died defending the Alamo in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: Davy Crockett was a frontiersman who died a hero at the Alamo.

clue.text: Sailor and social worker, in love, shooting American?

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
an ant is a social insect and a worker
love is zero in tennis, shown by O

explanation.surface: A sailor and a social worker fall in love, then something about an American shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooting here means filming, not firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is an American film director, and shooting is filming.

clue.text: Whitehall head once spoiled everything

indicators.note: something spoiled is wrecked, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A former head of Whitehall ruined it all.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the street of British government offices, used to mean the civil service.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole enchilada is an American idiom meaning all of it, everything.

clue.text: Terrible bane, this potent liqueur

indicators.note: terrible means in a bad state, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone calls a strong liqueur a dreadful curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, famously high in alcohol.

clue.text: Gets inside information: that should return savings

indicators.note: return means the combined letters are read backwards
inside puts gets within the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone obtains inside information that should pay off on savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside reads as part of the phrase inside information, but it is the insertion signal; that should return then turns the whole result round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money saved up for the future.

clue.text: Cricketer in pub outside Totnes regularly

indicators.note: the pub word goes outside the picked letters

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of Totnes

explanation.surface: A cricketer drinking in a pub on the outskirts of Totnes.
explanation.walkthrough: Totnes is a town in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter is the player who bats in cricket, a type of cricketer.

clue.text: Roman general in a thrilling production on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard, not as written

parts.note: a gripping show or book is a gripper

explanation.surface: A radio play about a Roman general is a thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech gripper ends like the final syllable of the general's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was a Roman general and close ally of Augustus.

clue.text: Cold chicken stuffed with duck son selected

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: stuffed with means the chicken holds the duck and son inside

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
a duck is zero in cricket, shown by O

explanation.surface: A cold roast chicken stuffed with duck, chosen by a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen is a past participle meaning picked out, the same as selected.

clue.text: Crew spotted cutter

parts.note: a band is a group or crew
saw means spotted, noticed

explanation.surface: A ship's crew sights a cutter, a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutter looks like a boat after crew; it is a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsaw is a power saw with a looped blade, a tool that cuts.

clue.text: 29 hero from East London region, that is

parts.note: Bow is a district in the East End of London
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A hero of clue 29 comes from a part of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 29 is ALAMO; Jim Bowie died defending it in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Bowie, of bowie knife fame, was a frontiersman who died at the Alamo.

clue.text: Talk tediously about old Queequeg's weapon

indicators.note: the talk phrase is placed about the old abbreviation

parts.note: to harp on is to talk tediously about something

explanation.surface: Someone droning on about an old harpooner's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Queequeg is the harpooner in Herman Melville's Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Queequeg the harpooner's tool is a barbed spear thrown at whales.

clue.text: Honshu port: good enough area encloses it

indicators.note: encloses means the outer letters wrap round the others

parts.note: OK means acceptable, good enough
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A Japanese port described as adequate, with an area around it.
explanation.walkthrough: It is old slang for sex appeal, which crosswords abbreviate SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city on Honshu, the main Japanese island.

clue.text: Mournful cry heard — is it Moby Dick?

indicators.note: heard means the word for the cry is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a wail is a long mournful cry

explanation.surface: Hearing a sad cry at sea, someone wonders if it is the famous white whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby Dick is the great white sperm whale in Melville's novel.

clue.text: Where fare goes down, Iago hopes when travelling

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Iago, the Shakespeare villain, hopes for good food on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The oesophagi are gullets, the tubes that swallowed food passes down; this is the plural form.

clue.text: Ivy for one always the ingenue?

parts.note: ever means always
an ingenue is naive and inexperienced, which is green

explanation.surface: Is a girl called Ivy forever the innocent young actress?
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of a plant that stays green.

clue.text: All lost after Mexican offensive — leaders herein?

definitions.text: All lost after Mexican offensive — leaders herein?

indicators.note: the leaders of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: All the defenders died after the Mexican assault, which is the story of the fort.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: in 1836 every defender of the Alamo died after the Mexican attack.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo is the Texas mission where all defenders were killed by a Mexican army in 1836.
